segments.arabic: [596] حدثنا أحمد بن يونس قال: حدثنا زهير قال: حدثنا سليمان التيمي عن أبي عثمان النهدي عن عبد الله بن مسعود عن النبي ﷺ قال
segments.english: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us. He said: Zuhayr related to us. He said: Sulayman al-Taymi related to us, from Abu ‘Uthman al-Nahdi, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Mas‘ud, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: لا يمنعن أحدكم أو أحدا منكم أذان بلال من سحوره فإنه يؤذن أو ينادي بليل ليرجع قائمكم ولينبه نائمكم وليس أن يقول الفجر أو الصبح، وقال بأصابعه ورفعها إلى فوق وطأطأ إلى أسفل حتى يقول هكذا،
segments.english: “Let Bilal’s adhan not prevent any one of you—or anyone among you—from his pre-dawn meal, for he gives the adhan—or calls—at night, so that those of you standing in prayer may return and those of you sleeping may awaken. Dawn—or morning—is not like this”—and he gestured with his fingers, raising them upwards and lowering them downwards—“until it is like this.”

segments.arabic: وقال زهير بسبابتيه إحداهما فوق الأخرى ثم مدها عن يمينه وشماله
segments.english: And Zuhayr gestured with his two index fingers, one above the other, then extended them to his right and left.

notes: All three source alternatives remain: any one of you/or anyone among you, gives the adhan/or calls, dawn/or morning. The finger movements and Zuhayr’s own demonstration remain. The Khan-family comparison labels the last demonstrator al-Zuhri; the selected Arabic and both prints name Zuhayr. Its added explanation of the horizon is not inserted. Al-‘Ayni explains the dawn phrase as a gesture, not merely an announcement that morning has begun. The historical print has an extra or before the waking clause; the selected digital and modern reading are retained.

segments.arabic: [597] حدثنا إسحاق قال: أخبرنا أبو أسامة قال عبيد الله حدثنا عن القاسم بن محمد عن عائشة وعن نافع عن ابن عمر أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Ishaq related to us. He said: Abu Usamah informed us. He said: ‘Ubayd Allah related to us, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from ‘A’ishah, and from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: ح وحدثني يوسف بن عيسى المروزي قال: حدثنا الفضل قال: حدثنا عبيد الله بن عمر عن القاسم بن محمد عن عائشة عن النبي ﷺ أنه قال
segments.english: Another chain: And Yusuf ibn ‘Isa al-Marwazi related to me. He said: al-Fadl related to us. He said: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Umar related to us, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from ‘A’ishah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, that he said:

segments.arabic: إن بلالا يؤذن بليل فكلوا واشربوا حتى يؤذن بن أم مكتوم
segments.english: “Bilal gives the adhan at night, so eat and drink until Ibn Umm Maktum gives the adhan.”

notes: Both complete chains remain, including the first route through ‘A’ishah and Ibn ‘Umar, its unfinished said, the ح switch, and the second first-person related to me formula. Another chain renders the source switch marker within the narrator section. The modern print numbers these routes 622 and 623; this is one selected digital entry. The historical print has related to us for Abu Usamah where the selected digital and modern print use informed us. Neither shortened English comparison replaces the chains.

segments.arabic: [598] حدثنا إسحاق الواسطي قال: حدثنا خالد عن الجريري عن ابن بريدة عن عبد الله بن مغفل المزني أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Ishaq al-Wasiti related to us. He said: Khalid related to us, from al-Jurayri, from Ibn Buraydah, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal al-Muzani, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: بين كل أذانين صلاة ثلاثا لمن شاء
segments.english: “Between every two calls there is a prayer”—three times—“for whoever wishes.”

notes: The selected wording says the phrase followed by three times and for whoever wishes. It is not expanded into three newly written repetitions. Bewley’s phrasing resembles the fuller repetition at 601. The dual adhans is rendered two calls; the adhan/iqamah context is in the chapter and source notes, not added as a parenthetical inside the report.

segments.arabic: [599] حدثنا محمد بن بشار قال: حدثنا غندر قال: حدثنا شعبة قال: سمعت عمرو بن عامر الأنصارى عن أنس بن مالك قال:
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us. He said: Ghundar related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us. He said: I heard ‘Amr ibn ‘Amir al-Ansari, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

segments.arabic: كان المؤذن إذا إذن قام ناس من أصحاب النبي ﷺ يبتدرون السواري حتى يخرج النبي ﷺ وهم كذلك يصلون الركعتين قبل المغرب ولم يكن بين الأذان والإقامة شيء
segments.english: When the caller gave the adhan, some Companions of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would stand and hurry towards the pillars, until the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out while they were like that, praying the two rak‘ahs before Maghrib. There was no interval between the adhan and the iqamah.

segments.arabic: قال عثمان بن جبلة وأبو داود عن شعبة لم يكن بينهما إلا قليل
segments.english: ‘Uthman ibn Jabalah and Abu Dawud said, from Shu‘bah: There was only a little between them.

notes: The body’s no interval and the separate transmission’s only a little remain distinct. Both English comparisons soften the body to a small interval and abbreviate the closing attribution. The selected source names ‘Uthman ibn Jabalah and Abu Dawud transmitting from Shu‘bah; all three names remain. The two selected honorifics remain at their own points.

segments.arabic: [600] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني عروة بن الزبير أن عائشة قالت
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that ‘A’ishah said:

segments.arabic: كان رسول الله ﷺ إذا سكت المؤذن بالأولى من صلاة الفجر قام فركع ركعتين خفيفتين قبل صلاة الفجر بعد أن يستبين الفجر ثم اضطجع على شقه الأيمن حتى يأتيه المؤذن للإقامة
segments.english: When the caller fell silent after the first call for the dawn prayer, the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would stand and pray two brief rak‘ahs before the dawn prayer, after dawn had become clear. Then he would lie on his right side until the caller came to him for the iqamah.

notes: The first call, dawn becoming clear, two brief rak‘ahs, lying on the right side and waiting for the caller remain in order. No account of the cause of the rest or extra instruction is added.

segments.arabic: [601] حدثنا عبد الله بن يزيد قال: حدثنا كهمس بن الحسن عن عبد الله بن بريدة عن عبد الله بن مغفل قال: قال النبي ﷺ
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yazid related to us. He said: Kahmas ibn al-Hasan related to us, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Buraydah, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal, who said: The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: بين كل أذانين صلاة بين كل أذانين صلاة، ثم قال في الثالثة لمن شاء
segments.english: “Between every two calls there is a prayer. Between every two calls there is a prayer.” Then he said on the third occasion: “For whoever wishes.”

notes: Both written repetitions and then on the third occasion remain exactly in their source form; a third full sentence is not reconstructed. The selected chain names Kahmas ibn al-Hasan and ‘Abd Allah ibn Buraydah completely.

segments.arabic: [602] حدثنا معلى بن أسد قال: حدثنا وهيب عن أيوب عن أبي قلابة عن مالك بن الحويرث
segments.english: Mu‘alla ibn Asad related to us. He said: Wuhayb related to us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Malik ibn al-Huwayrith:

segments.arabic: أتيت النبي ﷺ في نفر من قومي فأقمنا عنده عشرين ليلة وكان رحيما رفيقا فلما رأى شوقنا إلى أهالينا قال ارجعوا فكونوا فيهم وعلموهم وصلوا فإذا حضرت الصلاة فليؤذن لكم أحدكم وليؤمكم أكبركم
segments.english: I came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, with a group from my people, and we stayed with him for twenty nights. He was merciful and gentle. When he saw our longing for our families, he said: “Return and stay among them, teach them, and pray. When the time for prayer comes, let one of you give the adhan for you, and let the oldest of you lead you.”

notes: The twenty nights, the two qualities merciful and gentle, longing for families and all commands remain. The English comparison’s religion is not supplied after teach them; the selected wording does not specify that object.

segments.arabic: [603] حدثنا مسلم بن إبراهيم قال: حدثنا شعبة عن المهاجر أبي الحسن عن زيد بن وهب عن أبي ذر قال
segments.english: Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Shu‘bah related to us, from al-Muhajir Abu al-Hasan, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Abu Dharr, who said:

segments.arabic: كنا مع النبي ﷺ في سفر فأراد المؤذن أن يؤذن، فقال له أبرد ثم أراد أن يؤذن، فقال له أبرد ثم أراد أن يؤذن، فقال له أبرد حتى ساوى الظل التلول، فقال النبي ﷺ إن شدة الحر من فيح جهنم
segments.english: We were with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on a journey. The caller wanted to give the adhan, but he told him: “Wait until it is cooler.” Then he wanted to give the adhan, but he told him: “Wait until it is cooler.” Then he wanted to give the adhan, but he told him: “Wait until it is cooler,” until the shadow equalled the hillocks. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “The intensity of the heat is from the blast of Hell.”

notes: The selected digital and modern print repeat the cooling instruction three times; the historical print repeats it an additional time in the last clause. Three complete attempts and instructions remain in the selected working translation. The shadow equalling the hillocks is kept; an absent Zuhr label is not imported from the English comparison.

segments.arabic: [604] حدثنا محمد بن يوسف قال: حدثنا سفيان عن خالد الحذاء عن أبي قلابة عن مالك بن الحويرث قال
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from Khalid al-Hadhdha’, from Abu Qilabah, from Malik ibn al-Huwayrith, who said:

segments.arabic: أتى رجلان النبي ﷺ يريدان السفر، فقال النبي ﷺ إذا أنتما خرجتما فأذنا ثم أقيما ثم ليؤمكما أكبركما
segments.english: Two men came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, intending to travel. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “When you two set out, give the adhan, then the iqamah, then let the older of you lead you.”

notes: Both men, dual commands, sequence of adhan then iqamah, and the older of the two remain. Each of the two selected Prophet honorifics remains.

segments.arabic: [605] حدثنا محمد بن المثنى قال: حدثنا عبد الوهاب قال: حدثنا أيوب عن أبي قلابة قال: حدثنا مالك
segments.english: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Wahhab related to us. He said: Ayyub related to us, from Abu Qilabah, who said: Malik related to us:

segments.arabic: أتينا إلى النبي ﷺ ونحن شببة متقاربون فأقمنا عنده عشرين يوما وليلة وكان رسول الله ﷺ رحيما رفيقا فلما ظن أنا قد اشتهينا أهلنا أو قد اشتقنا سألنا عمن تركنا بعدنا فأخبرناه قال ارجعوا إلى أهليكم فأقيموا فيهم وعلموهم ومروهم
segments.english: We came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, as young men close in age, and stayed with him for twenty days and nights. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was merciful and gentle. When he thought that we had begun to long for our families—or yearn for them—he asked us about those we had left behind, and we told him. He said: “Return to your families, stay among them, teach them, and instruct them.”

segments.arabic: وذكر أشياء أحفظها أو لا أحفظها
segments.english: And he mentioned things which I remember—or do not remember.

segments.arabic: وصلوا كما رأيتموني أصلي فإذا حضرت الصلاة فليؤذن لكم أحدكم وليؤمكم أكبركم
segments.english: “And pray as you have seen me pray. When the time for prayer comes, let one of you give the adhan for you, and let the oldest of you lead you.”

notes: Both uncertainties remain: longing/or yearning and I remember/or do not remember. The memory remark stays a separate transmission note between the quoted instructions. Twenty days and nights and the question about those left behind remain. The historical print uses different direct-reporting formulas in the opening chain; the digital and modern wording remain selected. Explanatory objects religion and good things from the English comparison are not inserted.

segments.arabic: [606] حدثنا مسدد قال: أخبرنا يحيى عن عبيد الله بن عمر قال: حدثني نافع قال
segments.english: Musaddad related to us. He said: Yahya informed us, from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Umar, who said: Nafi‘ related to me. He said:

segments.arabic: إذن بن عمر في ليلة باردة بضجنان، ثم قال صلوا في رحالكم فأخبرنا أن رسول الله ﷺ كان يأمر مؤذنا يؤذن ثم يقول على إثره ألا صلوا في الرحال في الليلة الباردة أو المطيرة في السفر
segments.english: Ibn ‘Umar gave the adhan on a cold night at Dajnan, then said: “Pray in your dwellings.” He informed us that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to order a caller to give the adhan, then say immediately afterwards: “Pray in the dwellings,” on a cold or rainy night during a journey.

notes: The selected Yahya informed us and Nafi‘ related to me remain. The historical print uses a related-to-us formula for Yahya and a different connector before informed us; the modern witness agrees with the selected reading. Dajnan stays a place name; its geographical footnote is not narration. The cold-or-rainy qualification and travelling context remain.

segments.arabic: [607] حدثنا إسحاق قال: أخبرنا جعفر بن عون قال: حدثنا أبو العميس عن عون بن أبي جحيفة عن أبيه قال:
segments.english: Ishaq related to us. He said: Ja‘far ibn ‘Awn informed us. He said: Abu al-‘Umays related to us, from ‘Awn ibn Abi Juhayfah, from his father, who said:

segments.arabic: رأيت رسول الله ﷺ بالأبطح فجاءه بلال فآذنه بالصلاة ثم خرج بلال بالعنزة حتى ركزها بين يدي رسول الله ﷺ بالأبطح وأقام الصلاة
segments.english: I saw the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, at al-Abtah. Bilal came to him and informed him of the prayer. Then Bilal came out with the short spear and planted it before the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, at al-Abtah, and gave the iqamah.

notes: The verb فآذنه بالصلاة is rendered informed him of the prayer, as in the Khan-family comparison, rather than Bewley’s gave the adhan. The later iqamah, short spear and both occurrences of al-Abtah remain. Both selected honorifics remain.

segments.arabic: [608] حدثنا محمد بن يوسف قال: حدثنا سفيان عن عون بن أبي جحيفة عن أبيه
segments.english: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Sufyan related to us, from ‘Awn ibn Abi Juhayfah, from his father:

segments.arabic: أنه رأى بلالا يؤذن فجعلت أتتبع فاه هاهنا وهاهنا بالأذان
segments.english: That he saw Bilal giving the adhan: I began following his mouth this way and that as he gave the adhan.

notes: The report preserves its shift from he saw to I began following his mouth. It is not reduced to a third-person observation that Bilal turned his face, as in the English comparisons. segments.arabic: [609] حدثنا أبو نعيم قال: حدثنا شيبان عن يحيى عن عبد الله بن أبي قتادة عن أبيه قال
segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Shayban related to us, from Yahya, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, who said:

segments.arabic: بينما نحن نصلي مع النبي ﷺ إذ سمع جلبة رجال فلما صلى قال: ما شأنكم قالوا استعجلنا إلى الصلاة قال: فلا تفعلوا إذا أتيتم الصلاة فعليكم بالسكينة فما أدركتم فصلوا وما فاتكم فأتموا
segments.english: While we were praying with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he heard a commotion of men. When he had prayed, he said: “What is the matter with you?” They said: “We hurried to the prayer.” He said: “Do not do that. When you come to prayer, be calm. Pray what you catch, and complete what you have missed.”

notes: The chain is ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Qatadah from his father, not Abu Qatadah from his father as in the shortened Bewley opening. The commotion, question, answer, prohibition and both catch/complete clauses remain.

segments.arabic: [610] حدثنا آدم قال: حدثنا ابن أبي ذئب قال: حدثنا الزهري عن سعيد بن المسيب عن أبي هريرة عن النبي ﷺ وعن الزهري عن أبي سلمة عن أبي هريرة عن النبي ﷺ قال:
segments.english: Adam related to us. He said: Ibn Abi Dhi’b related to us. He said: al-Zuhri related to us, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; and from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:

segments.arabic: إذا سمعتم الإقامة فامشوا إلى الصلاة وعليكم بالسكينة والوقار ولا تسرعوا فما أدركتم فصلوا وما فاتكم فأتموا
segments.english: “When you hear the iqamah, walk to prayer with calmness and dignity, and do not hurry. Pray what you catch, and complete what you have missed.”

notes: Both complete routes through al-Zuhri remain, one through Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab and one through Abu Salamah. Both honorifics remain. The selected digital source has no ح at the route change, though the historical print inserts one; no marker is invented in the selected Arabic or English.

segments.arabic: [611] حدثنا مسلم بن إبراهيم قال: حدثنا هشام قال كتب إلي يحيى عن عبد الله بن أبي قتادة عن أبيه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
segments.english: Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us. He said: Hisham related to us. He said: Yahya wrote to me, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: إذا أقيمت الصلاة فلا تقوموا حتى تروني
segments.english: “When the iqamah has been given, do not stand until you see me.”

notes: Yahya wrote to me remains a written transmission; it is not generalized to a spoken report. The historical print expands Yahya to Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, while the selected digital and modern print retain the shorter name. No in-front-of-you parenthesis from the comparison is added.

segments.arabic: [612] حدثنا أبو نعيم قال: حدثنا شيبان عن يحيى عن عبد الله بن أبي قتادة عن أبيه قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ:
segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Shayban related to us, from Yahya, from ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: إذا أقيمت الصلاة فلا تقوموا حتى تروني وعليكم بالسكينة
segments.english: “When the iqamah has been given, do not stand until you see me, and remain calm.”

segments.arabic: تابعه علي بن المبارك
segments.english: ‘Ali ibn al-Mubarak followed him in transmitting this.

It is transcribed without vowel marks as a distinct printed addition, translated as a separate transmission note and exposed in source context. The original digital paragraph remains unchanged.

segments.arabic: [613] حدثنا عبد العزيز بن عبد الله قال: حدثنا إبراهيم بن سعد عن صالح بن كيسان عن ابن شهاب عن أبي سلمة عن أبي هريرة
segments.english: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd Allah related to us. He said: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d related to us, from Salih ibn Kaysan, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah:

segments.arabic: أن رسول الله ﷺ خرج وقد أقيمت الصلاة وعدلت الصفوف حتى إذا قام في مصلاه انتظرنا أن يكبر انصرف قال على مكانكم فمكثنا على هيئتنا حتى خرج إلينا ينطف رأسه ماء وقد اغتسل
segments.english: That the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out after the iqamah had been given and the rows had been straightened. When he stood in his prayer place, we waited for him to say the takbir. He turned back and said: “Stay where you are.” We remained as we were until he came out to us with water dripping from his head; he had bathed.

notes: The first came out does not become went out of the mosque: that direction is not specified in the selected Arabic. Waiting for the takbir, turning back, remaining in place and water dripping from his head remain. No cause for the bath is supplied from the comparison parenthesis.

segments.arabic: [614] حدثنا إسحاق قال: حدثنا محمد بن يوسف قال: حدثنا الأوزاعي عن الزهري عن أبي سلمة بن عبد الرحمن عن أبي هريرة قال
segments.english: Ishaq related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: al-Awza‘i related to us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, who said:

segments.arabic: أقيمت الصلاة فسوى الناس صفوفهم فخرج رسول الله ﷺ فتقدم وهو جنب، ثم قال على مكانكم فرجع فاغتسل ثم خرج ورأسه يقطر ماء فصلى بهم
segments.english: The iqamah was given, and the people straightened their rows. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, came out and went forward while he was in a state of janabah. Then he said: “Stay where you are.” He returned and bathed, then came out with his head dripping water and led them in prayer.

notes: The source explicitly says a state of janabah here, unlike the preceding selected report. The returning, bathing, emerging and leading prayer remain. The historical print uses informed us for Muhammad ibn Yusuf; the selected digital and modern print use related to us.

segments.arabic: [615] حدثنا أبو نعيم قال: حدثنا شيبان عن يحيى قال: سمعت أبا سلمة يقول أخبرنا جابر بن عبد الله
segments.english: Abu Nu‘aym related to us. He said: Shayban related to us, from Yahya, who said: I heard Abu Salamah say: Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah informed us:

segments.arabic: أن النبي ﷺ جاءه عمر بن الخطاب يوم الخندق، فقال: يا رسول الله والله ما كدت أن أصلي حتى كادت الشمس تغرب وذلك بعد ما أفطر الصائم، فقال النبي ﷺ والله ما صليتها فنزل النبي ﷺ إلى بطحان وأنا معه فتوضأ ثم صلى يعني العصر بعد ما غربت الشمس ثم صلى بعدها المغرب
segments.english: That ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, on the Day of the Trench and said: “Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I had scarcely managed to pray before the sun was about to set.” That was after the fasting person had broken his fast. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “By Allah, I have not prayed it.” The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, went down to Buthan, and I was with him. He performed ablution and then prayed—meaning ‘Asr—after the sun had set, then prayed Maghrib after it.

notes: The selected Arabic retains both scarcely/about-to constructions, the statement that this occurred after the fasting person broke his fast, all three honorifics, the Prophet’s oath and the narrator’s meaning ‘Asr. Bewley adds cursing Quraysh not present here; the pinned Khan-family comparison omits the Prophet’s oath. Neither difference is silently imported. The historical print directly names ‘Asr in the final clause while the digital and modern print retain the narrator’s means ‘Asr aside.

segments.arabic: [616] حدثنا أبو معمر عبد الله بن عمرو قال: حدثنا عبد الوارث قال: حدثنا عبد العزيز بن صهيب عن أنس قال
segments.english: Abu Ma‘mar ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amr related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Warith related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Suhayb related to us, from Anas, who said:

segments.arabic: أقيمت الصلاة والنبي ﷺ يناجي رجلا في جانب المسجد فما قام إلى الصلاة حتى نام القوم
segments.english: The iqamah was given while the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was speaking privately to a man at the side of the mosque. He did not stand for prayer until the people had fallen asleep.

notes: The full Abu Ma‘mar ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amr name, private conversation, side of the mosque and until the people slept remain. The comparison’s some and sitting-posture explanation are not added. The historical print inserts هو before Ibn Suhayb; selected digital and modern wording remain.

segments.arabic: [617] حدثنا عياش بن الوليد قال: حدثنا عبد الأعلى قال: حدثنا حميد
segments.english: ‘Ayyash ibn al-Walid related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-A‘la related to us. He said: Humayd related to us.

segments.arabic: قال: سألت ثابتا البناني عن الرجل يتكلم بعد ما تقام الصلاة فحدثني عن أنس بن مالك قال
segments.english: He said: I asked Thabit al-Bunani about a man speaking after the iqamah had been given. He related to me, from Anas ibn Malik, who said:

segments.arabic: أقيمت الصلاة فعرض للنبي ﷺ رجل فحبسه بعد ما أقيمت الصلاة
segments.english: The iqamah was given, and a man approached the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and detained him after the iqamah had been given.

notes: Humayd’s full question to Thabit al-Bunani and the ensuing Anas report remain, as does the repeated after-the-iqamah clause. The modern print additionally repeats al-Hasan’s statement adjacent to this entry; the selected digital source and historical print place it under the following chapter. That chapter material remains separate and is not folded into the narration.

segments.arabic: [618] حدثنا عبد الله بن يوسف قال: أخبرنا مالك عن أبي الزناد عن الأعرج عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ قال:
segments.english: ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A‘raj, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

segments.arabic: والذي نفسي بيده لقد هممت أن آمر بحطب فيحطب ثم آمر بالصلاة فيؤذن لها ثم آمر رجلا فيؤم الناس ثم أخالف إلى رجال فأحرق عليهم بيوتهم والذي نفسي بيده لو يعلم أحدهم أنه يجد عرقا سمينا أو مرماتين حسنتين لشهد العشاء
segments.english: “By Him in whose hand is my soul, I considered ordering firewood to be gathered, then ordering the prayer and having its adhan called, then ordering a man to lead the people, then going to some men and burning their houses down upon them. By Him in whose hand is my soul, if one of them knew that he would find a meaty bone or two good pieces of meat from between a sheep’s hooves, he would attend ‘Isha’.”

notes: Both oaths and the complete sequence of contemplated actions remain; no action is changed from contemplated to performed. The source does not append an explanatory non-attendance clause to some men. The two English comparisons differ on مرماتين: Bewley gives hooves, while the pinned Khan-family text gives meat between ribs. Ibn Hajar records meat between sheep’s hooves and an alternative arrows interpretation. The working rendering selects the former lexical sense with an explicit uncertainty notice. No ruling or reader instruction is supplied by the app.
